title.en: What Kind of Museum Visitor Are You?
title.zh: 逛博物馆时，你会怎样看？

description.en: Six exhibit choices reveal your visiting rhythm: looking closely, following connections, or making meaning together. Free portraits for a more personal museum day.
description.zh: 6道展览情境题，看看你偏向细看一件、追踪关联，还是与人共同理解。免费获得更贴近自己的观展画像。

introduction.en: Imagine a museum or small local exhibition where you can choose your route. There is no knowledge test. Reading every label, enjoying the room, or sharing a conversation are different ways to visit, not a ranking of cultural sophistication.
introduction.zh: 想象一场可以自主选择路线的博物馆或本地小展览。这里不考知识。读标签、感受空间或与同行者聊聊，都是不同的参观方式，不是文化品位的高低排名。

focus.en: Where you place attention when the collection offers more objects and stories than you can take in at once.
focus.zh: 展品与故事比一次能看完的更多时，你会把注意力放在哪里。

prompt.en: You have one hour in an unfamiliar exhibition. You start by…
prompt.zh: 第一次看这个展，只有一小时，你会先……

label.en: Choosing one object that makes me want to stop.
label.zh: 找一件让我想停下来的展品。

label.en: Looking at the room map and the exhibition’s main thread.
label.zh: 看看平面图和整个展览的主线。

label.en: Asking my companion what they are drawn to.
label.zh: 问问同行者先被什么吸引。

prompt.en: An object has a long label and an intriguing surface. You…
prompt.zh: 一件展品有很长的说明，表面细节也很有趣，你会……

label.en: Follow the label to its links with other objects.
label.zh: 顺着说明，看看它和其他展品的关联。

label.en: Spend time with its visible details before reading more.
label.zh: 先留意看得见的细节，再决定读多少。

label.en: Compare what each of us noticed first.
label.zh: 和同行者比比，刚才先注意到什么。

prompt.en: Which moment would you most like to remember afterward?
prompt.zh: 离开展览后，你最想记住哪种瞬间？

label.en: An unexpected conversation prompted by one exhibit.
label.zh: 一件展品引出的一段意外对话。

label.en: A tiny detail I would have missed if I hurried.
label.zh: 一个走快了就会错过的微小细节。

label.en: The way several rooms changed my view of one theme.
label.zh: 几个展厅怎样逐步改变我对同一主题的理解。

prompt.en: A popular gallery is crowded. You prefer to…
prompt.zh: 热门展厅有点挤，你更想……

label.en: Find a quieter related room and continue the same story.
label.zh: 去安静些的相关展厅，接着看这条线。

label.en: Choose one less crowded object and stay with it.
label.zh: 挑一件不那么挤的展品，认真看一会儿。

label.en: Check whether my companion wants to split up and meet later.
label.zh: 问问同行者是否想分开看，稍后再集合。

prompt.en: You encounter something you do not understand. You…
prompt.zh: 遇到一件暂时看不懂的东西，你会……

label.en: Ask a companion what questions it gives them.
label.zh: 问同行者，它让你想到什么问题。

label.en: Look again and list what I can actually see.
label.zh: 再看一遍，先确认自己实际看见了什么。

label.en: Look for the curator’s explanation or a neighboring comparison.
label.zh: 找找策展说明或附近可供对照的展品。

prompt.en: There is time for one final stop. You choose…
prompt.zh: 最后还够看一处，你会选……

label.en: A room that completes a connection I have been following.
label.zh: 能补上我一直追踪的关联的展厅。

label.en: An object I want to spend a little more time with.
label.zh: 一件还想多待一会儿的展品。

label.en: A place where we can talk about what stayed with us.
label.zh: 一个能聊聊各自印象的地方。

summary.en: Your museum choices favor depth of attention over the number of rooms covered. You want an encounter long enough for details to emerge. One object can make a visit feel complete without representing the whole collection.
summary.zh: 你的观展选择偏向注意力的深度，而不是走过多少个展厅。你希望和一件东西相处久一点，让细节浮现。一次参观可以因为一件展品而完整，却不必由它代表整个馆藏。

example.en: You might spend several minutes with a worn handle, a brushstroke, or an unexpected texture, then read enough to distinguish your observation from the object’s documented story.
example.zh: 你可能花几分钟留意磨损的把手、一道笔触或意外的肌理，再读一点说明，分清自己的观察与展品已有记录的故事。

strength.en: You notice specifics and give an object space to be more than a label. This makes room for questions that a quick overview may miss.
strength.zh: 你会注意具体之处，让展品不只是一张标签。这样的停留，也给概览中容易错过的问题留下空间。

tradeoff.en: A powerful encounter with one object cannot stand in for the history of an entire place or people. Context can change an attractive first impression.
tradeoff.zh: 一件展品带来的强烈感受，不能替代整个地区或人群的历史。补上背景后，最初的印象也可能改变。

experiment.en: Choose one object on your next visit and note one detail plus one question. Read its source label before deciding what your observation might mean.
experiment.zh: 下次挑一件展品，记一个细节和一个问题。在判断观察意味着什么之前，先看看它的来源说明。

summary.en: You enjoy seeing how objects speak to one another across a room or theme. Your portrait favors a route with connections: changes in use, contrasting interpretations, or an idea that grows from gallery to gallery. You do not need to finish every room to follow a useful thread.
summary.zh: 你喜欢看展品怎样跨越房间或主题相互回应。你的画像偏向有连接的路线：用途的改变、不同解释的对照，或随着展厅推进而逐渐展开的想法。不必看完每个房间，也能追到一条有意思的线。

example.en: A tool in the first room may change how you understand an object in the last. You might return briefly to compare them, rather than treating the exhibition as a checklist of independent highlights.
example.zh: 第一间的工具，可能改变你对最后一间某件物品的理解。你也许会短暂折返比较，而不把展览当成彼此独立的打卡点。

strength.en: You can connect details to a larger question and make the exhibition easier to describe afterward. A clear thread can organize a complex visit.
strength.zh: 你能把细节接回一个较大的问题，也更容易在离开后讲清这次展览。一条清楚的线索，可以帮助整理复杂的参观体验。

tradeoff.en: The curator’s route is one interpretation, not the only possible story. Following it too tightly can make surprising details seem irrelevant before you have looked.
tradeoff.zh: 策展路线是一种解释，不是唯一可能的故事。跟得太紧时，意外细节也可能在你细看之前就被判定为无关。

experiment.en: Follow one exhibition question, then deliberately stop at an object that seems not to fit. Ask what additional context would help you understand the contrast.
experiment.zh: 下次可以追踪一个展览问题，再有意停在一件似乎不合这条线的展品前。想想还缺哪些背景，才能理解这个对照。

summary.en: You enjoy a visit that makes room for another person’s attention alongside your own. A companion’s question or memory can open a different way into an object. The point is shared exploration, not having to agree on what the exhibition means.
summary.zh: 你喜欢让自己的注意力与另一个人的注意力并排出现。同行者的问题或记忆，可能给一件展品打开另一种入口。重点是共同探索，不必对展览的意义达成一致。

example.en: One person notices a material while another remembers a similar object at home. Talking about both can enrich the visit, provided that guesses remain separate from the museum’s documented facts.
example.zh: 一个人注意材料，另一个人想起家里的类似物件。聊聊两者能丰富参观，但仍要把猜想与馆方记录的事实分开。

strength.en: You invite different observations and make visiting feel accessible to people who do not share the same prior knowledge. A good question can include someone without testing them.
strength.zh: 你愿意接纳不同观察，也让知识背景不同的人更容易一起看展。一个好问题可以邀请参与，而不是考查对方。

tradeoff.en: A companion may want silence or a different pace. Shared meaning grows more comfortably when you can spend part of the visit apart and meet again.
tradeoff.zh: 同行者也可能想安静，或想用不同速度看。能够分开看一会儿再会合时，共同理解反而更自在。

experiment.en: Ask one open question at the next exhibition, then agree on a short independent stretch. Compare one observation afterward without trying to choose a winning interpretation.
experiment.zh: 下次看展时，先问一个开放的问题，再约一小段各自参观。回来交流一个观察，不必选出谁的解释最好。
